title: Annotate genomic intervals by overlap
repo_revision: master retrieved 2026-09-29; commit SHA unavailable in inspected public metadata

sources.locator: # bedtools intersect rendered source: default, -wa/-wb, -wo, -c, -v, overlap fractions, strand, multiple B files
# intersect; usage and options; overlap fraction, strand, sorted algorithm sections

scientific_use: Compare genomic feature sets to identify overlaps, report the overlapping records or overlap lengths, count annotations per query, select non-overlapping queries, or require fractional and strand-aware overlap. Tutorial examples annotate CpG islands with exons and compare exons to CpG, GWAS, and ChromHMM features.
tool_role_basis: The tutorial invokes bedtools intersect as a CLI on BED records; it consumes interval inputs and reports genomic relationships rather than implementing the overlap algorithm in tutorial code.

inputs.meaning: Query feature intervals (A), e.g. CpG islands or exons
inputs.format: BED; docs also state BAM/GFF/VCF inputs

inputs.meaning: Comparison feature intervals (B), e.g. exons, GWAS loci, ChromHMM states

outputs.meaning: Overlapping or non-overlapping query features, paired records, overlap bp, or per-query overlap counts depending on flags

dependencies: Coordinate-compatible interval files; for -sorted, both inputs grouped and position-sorted; optional genome file defines chromosome order
limitations: Tutorial command outputs are illustrative; no execution was performed.
Inputs are described as tutorial downloads from a historical UVA lab URL; current availability, genome build, exact file revisions, and redistribution terms are unverified.
A task author must choose a biological question and expected overlap semantics/flags.

scientific_use: Collapse overlapping exon or repeat intervals into contiguous genomic regions, optionally summarize the number and names of contributing records, or merge features within a specified distance.
tool_role_basis: Examples call bedtools merge on exon BED records and use its count/collapse aggregations; the source demonstrates scientific data processing with the utility.

inputs.meaning: Exon or repetitive-element intervals to consolidate
inputs.stage: individual annotated genomic intervals; input must be sorted by chromosome and start

outputs.meaning: Merged genomic intervals, optionally with feature counts or collapsed source names

dependencies: bedtools CLI; sorted input; choose distance threshold and aggregation columns/operators
limitations: The biological interpretation of merging exon records across transcript isoforms is not specified; merged intervals may discard transcript-level distinctions.
No execution or inspection of the referenced exons BED data was performed.

scientific_use: Quantify how much of each chromosome/genome is covered by intervals or aligned reads, and produce per-base or run-length encoded coverage tracks that can identify uncovered or high-depth regions.
tool_role_basis: Tutorial and reference documentation use bedtools genomecov to transform BED or BAM records into coverage histograms, per-base depths, or BEDGRAPH output.

inputs.meaning: Feature intervals or mapped reads whose coverage is measured
Chromosome names and lengths defining coverage universe

outputs.meaning: Coverage depth histogram, per-base coverage, or BEDGRAPH intervals; zero-depth intervals available with -bga

dependencies: bedtools CLI; BED/GFF/VCF input must be chromosome-grouped and requires genome file; reference chromosome names and lengths must match
limitations: Tutorial output is illustrative and not executed.
The tutorial's genome file assembly/version and the relationship of all example BED inputs to it are not established.
Large BAM coverage jobs may have material I/O and output-size requirements; runtime is unmeasured.

title: Compare DNase hypersensitivity interval sets
repo_revision: master retrieved 2026-09-29; commit SHA unavailable in inspected public metadata

sources.locator: # Principal component analysis and # A Jaccard statistic for all 400 pairwise comparisons
Summary and citation; genomic interval set operations and composable command line

scientific_use: Compute base-pair Jaccard similarity among DNase hypersensitivity peak interval sets from fetal heart and skin fibroblast samples, then organize 400 pairwise comparisons into a matrix for hierarchical clustering or PCA to inspect tissue-level similarity.
tool_role_basis: The workflow uses bedtools jaccard to compute interval similarity, then shell utilities, GNU parallel, a downloaded Python matrix script, and R/ggplot2/RColorBrewer to assemble and visualize comparisons.

inputs.meaning: Merged DNase hypersensitivity hotspot intervals for 20 fetal tissue samples; examples identify fetal heart and skin fibroblast samples
inputs.stage: processed peak sets, merged and FDR-filtered; filenames specify hg19 for one example

outputs.meaning: Pairwise base-pair Jaccard values, named distance/similarity matrix, and downstream clustered or PCA visualization

limitations: The tutorial attributes its broader biological context to Maurano et al. 2012 and describes DNase hypersensitivity across primary tissues; exact sample manifest, all 20 file URLs, and processing provenance were not inspected.
A 20x20 similarity matrix is not itself PCA or hierarchical clustering; the tutorial leaves downstream analysis as a proposed use.
GNU parallel is configured to use as many processors as available; resource limits and reproducibility controls must be set by a task author.
No task execution or biological conclusion was validated.

title: Extract interval or spliced transcript sequences from a reference

scientific_use: Extract nucleotide sequences for genomic intervals from a reference FASTA; optionally use feature names in headers, orient by strand, or concatenate BED12 blocks to produce spliced transcript sequences.
tool_role_basis: Documentation specifies bedtools getfasta CLI input reference FASTA plus BED/GFF/VCF and output FASTA or tabular sequences.

inputs.meaning: Reference genome sequence and interval features; FASTA header contig names must exactly match interval chromosome field
inputs.format: FASTA and BED/GFF/VCF; BED12 for block concatenation

outputs.meaning: Sequence for each input interval, optionally reverse complemented or concatenated across blocks

dependencies: Reference assembly matching interval coordinates and contig names
Strand field for -s; BED12 block definitions for -split
limitations: Documentation examples use tiny in-page FASTA and BED snippets, which are illustrative inputs rather than an identified reusable biological dataset.
No reference assembly, biological feature dataset, or downstream sequence analysis is specified.
